jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Stream

Stream powers real-time Chat, Video, Activity Feeds, and AI Moderation for more than 1 billion end users across 4,000+ apps, from Strava and Bumble to eBay and Patreon. Our platform processes billions of API requests per month and supports applications with millions of concurrent users, while delivering highly reliable, low-latency services and a great developer experience.

The role

We're looking for a Solutions Consultant II, Trust & Safety to join Stream on our mission of elevating the quality of apps for billions of users globally. You'll own the customer side of our AI Moderation product: getting new customers live, keeping their setup accurate as their communities change, and making their moderation teams fast and confident in the product.

This is a full-time, remote role for people based in the US in the Mountain, Central or Eastern time zone.

What you'll work on

AI Moderation is one of the fastest-growing parts of Stream. Customers use it to detect harmful text, images, video and audio in real time, set up policies and automated actions, and review what's left in a moderation queue their teams work in every day. You'll report to our GTM Lead for AI Moderation and own each customer's journey from late-stage deals and pilots, through onboarding, to the ongoing relationship. Sales and Solutions Engineering own the deal with you alongside them. Our engineers own the detection models themselves. You own whether each customer's configuration actually works for their community. Many of our customers don't have an in-house Trust & Safety team, so you'll often be the most experienced moderation person in the room. There's no settled onboarding playbook yet, so you'll build it.

Job responsibilities

  • Run onboarding end to end: kickoff, policy design, configuration, testing and go-live, with a clear go-live bar agreed with each customer and both sides kept aligned on timeline and open items.

  • Turn guidelines into configuration: translate a customer's written community guidelines into policies, harm categories, thresholds, blocklists and automated actions in the Stream dashboard.

  • Tune customer setups: review flagged and missed content, find where a customer's configuration causes false positives or misses, and adjust it to improve precision and recall.

  • Own escalations: when moderation behaves unexpectedly, dig into flagged content and API responses, and work with our engineers to get to the root cause.

  • Support integrations: help customer engineering teams with API questions, webhook setup and getting moderation events into their own systems.

  • Enable customer teams: train moderators and T&S leads on the review queue, dashboard, rule builder and reporting, and build the playbooks, vertical templates and tuning checklists that make onboarding repeatable.

  • Show the value: run check-ins and business reviews that tie moderation results to each customer's own goals, support renewals and expansion, and bring prioritized, evidence-backed customer needs to Product.

About you

You like owning the whole customer relationship, from the first configuration call to the business review a year later. You're technical enough to read an API response and explain why a rule fired, but you don't want to write production code. You keep several projects moving at once and you're honest about where each one stands. You'll work closely with our engineering team in Europe, so you'll need regular overlap with European morning hours. This role means reviewing harmful content, including harassment, hate speech and NSFW imagery, as part of tuning and diagnosis. We take reviewer wellbeing seriously and will talk about it openly in the process. If you want a defined process to follow, or prefer a narrow role in a large CS team, this probably isn't the right fit.

You have

  • 3+ years in a customer-facing role at a technical or SaaS company: customer success, implementation, solutions consulting, technical account management, professional services, or Trust & Safety operations with external stakeholders.

  • A working understanding of APIs and webhooks, enough to answer basic integration questions without pulling in an engineer. No coding required.

  • Strong project management: you can run several onboardings in parallel and keep each one on track.

  • An analytical habit: you answer "is this actually working?" with data.

  • Clear written and spoken communication, whether you're training a room of moderators or presenting to a customer's leadership.

  • Willingness to review difficult and harmful content as part of the job.

Bonus points

  • Direct Trust & Safety, content moderation or community operations experience, in-house at a platform, at a BPO or vendor, or at a moderation tooling company.

  • Familiarity with policy taxonomies, harm categories, precision and recall tradeoffs, appeals, and CSAM reporting obligations.

  • Working knowledge of online safety regulation such as the DSA, OSA, COPPA and the EU AI Act.

  • Experience with chat, social, gaming, marketplace or dating platforms.

  • Experience building enablement content or customer-facing documentation from scratch.

What makes this role exciting

  • You're an early hire on the customer side of AI Moderation, so you'll shape how onboarding and tuning work instead of inheriting a process.

  • Your work is visible: Trust & Safety leaders decide whether to buy and renew based on how good onboarding and tuning are.

  • Within your first year, the goal is for most of our moderation customers to be in a regular rhythm of check-ins with you, with you owning retention for the moderation book.

  • You'll work hands-on in Stream's moderation dashboard, rule builder, review queue, APIs and webhooks.

Why join Stream?

We're a Series B company with offices in Boulder, Amsterdam, Skopje and Toronto, and a team of 140+ people from 37 nationalities. We're backed by Felicis Ventures, GGV Capital, 01 Advisors, Techstars, and Arthur Ventures, with angels including Dick Costolo (ex-CEO of Twitter), Olivier Pomel (CEO of Datadog), Tom Preston-Werner (co-founder of GitHub), and Nicolas Dessaigne (co-founder of Algolia).

We'll be straight with you: a startup is more demanding than a large company. There's no fixed playbook, you'll own things end to end, and you'll sometimes pick up work outside your title. That's also what makes it a fast place to grow. If you want real ownership and high scale more than structure and a set career ladder, you'll feel at home here.

What we have to offer you

Note: this list of benefits applies to Colorado-based employees and is adjusted per your location of residence.

Stream employees enjoy some of the best job benefits in the industry:

  • 19+ days of paid time off plus 10 paid holidays

  • Free health insurance for the employee and partial coverage for dependents (80% contribution coverage for health and 100% for dental and vision)

  • 401k contribution plan with 4% match

  • Fitness stipend

  • Company equity

  • Dog-friendly office!

  • A Macbook Pro provided

  • A Learning and Development budget

  • Team lunches and plenty of snacks

  • RTD pass + free parking pass on Pearl Street

  • An office on Pearl Street in downtown Boulder

  • 12 weeks paid parental leave for primary parents

  • The opportunity to attend or present to global conferences and meetups

  • The possibility to visit our office in Amsterdam

Salary (for Colorado only): Our salary ranges are based on national averages. We have wide ranges so we can be flexible and determine compensation based on a number of factors including the candidate's skills, level of experience, and location. For Colorado-based candidates, the salary range for this position is $100k -130k On target earnings. Compensation at all other locations will be based on the factors as stated above.

Our culture

Stream has a casual social culture, our team is diverse and we all have different backgrounds. Now, Stream is a team of over 140+ peers from over 35 countries across the globe.

We value transparency, aim for excellence, and support each other on our way to new victories.

Our team consists of the strongest talents all over the world, which makes Stream a great place to learn and improve your skills.

When it comes to software engineering jobs, our culture is oriented towards ownership and quality: our goal is to deliver stable software.

If you are interested in becoming a part of what we do, apply for this vacancy now!

Hybrid office policy: applicants based (or relocating to) one of our office locations are expected to work according to the applicable local office attendance policy.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Staff Software Engineer, Platform & Infrastructure

The role

We are hiring a Staff Software Engineer for our Infrastructure team.

Stream runs behind apps that more than a billion people use: billions of API requests a month, a 99.999% uptime promise, and a small team keeping it all running. Infrastructure here decides how fast our products feel, how well they scale, and how quickly we can launch new ones.

This year we're wrapping up a big move. We're simplifying where and how we host, and rebuilding our data layer on self-hosted, open-source systems that are faster and cheaper to run. That's the groundwork, not the job. Next comes building the infrastructure every Stream product runs on, including the ones we haven't built yet. That means real SLOs, clear costs, calmer on-call, and a platform that helps teams ship faster.

What you build will shape how much Stream spends and how fast it grows, and we'll trust you with big decisions from your first few weeks.

This is a Software Engineering role first. Attitude, ambition and a willingness to experiment across the stack matter more to us than years of Kubernetes or database operations. We expect AI to cover a good share of the DevOps-heavy work, and we expect you to use it that way. What a tool can't give us is system design judgement, strong fundamentals and good code, so that is what we look for.

Platform & Infrastructure is a small, senior team without the support structures of a large organisation. It moves fast and it gets hectic. We would rather say that now than have you find out in month two.

 

What team is focusing on:

  • Runs Stream's global platform. Keeps the edge and backend that serve customers worldwide fast and up, at single-digit millisecond latency on a 99.999% uptime SLA.

  • Shapes Stream's margins. Our hosting and infrastructure decisions directly drive the company's profitability. You will decide where and how we run, and what we stop paying for.

  • Builds tools people actually want to use. Internal tools that change how engineers deploy and debug, and external ones that give customers a clear view of their own traffic and health.

  • Makes on-call boring. Builds a rotation people can sustain, and cuts alert noise until a page means something real is broken.

  • Makes cost visible. Gives every team a clear view of what it spends on infrastructure and why, so cost becomes part of every engineering decision.

What you will do:

  • Define what "good" looks like for the platform. Set latency and uptime SLOs for every product team, and decide what we measure, from error rates and delivery times to how healthy our customers' apps really are.

  • Make the big infrastructure calls. Lead the design reviews and decisions on where and how we run, working with backend, video and moderation engineers on tradeoffs that cross service boundaries.

  • Build the platform tooling. Write the internal tools and services that help engineers ship, deploy and debug faster, plus the docs and AI skills that make launching a new product repeatable.

  • Turn incidents into fixes that stick. Take part in on-call, and make sure every root cause ends in a durable fix, not a workaround.

  • Make cost part of every design. Weigh cost alongside reliability in every decision, and give teams the numbers to do the same.

What we are looking for:

  • A software engineer who has built systems, not only configured them. You write production code in Go, Python or a similar language. Scripting-only backgrounds are not a fit.

  • Strong system design. You can reason about failure modes, capacity and cost in distributed systems, and explain why you chose what you chose.

  • Solid fundamentals in networking, storage and concurrency, and the habit of asking why a system behaves the way it does instead of accepting the default.

  • You have owned high-scale production systems and set technical direction beyond your own work, through design reviews, RFCs and decisions other engineers build on.

  • You experiment. When you hit Kubernetes, a database or a cloud service you have not run before, you dig in, use AI to close the gap, and ship.

  • You already use AI tools every day in your engineering work.

  • You treat cost and reliability as engineering problems, and you can put a number on an outcome you drove.

  • You write clearly. Much of this role is docs and standards that other teams will follow.

  • You are comfortable in a small team, setting direction and reviewing a PR in the same week.

Nice to have experience:

  • Kubernetes in production: cluster architecture, workload design or a migration you led.

  • PostgreSQL at scale, ideally self-hosted or with CloudNativePG: sharding, replication, partitioning tradeoffs.

  • Valkey or Redis at scale, ideally on Kubernetes.

  • Hands-on AWS and GCP, including multi-cloud setups or migrations between providers.

  • Cloud commitment and reservation strategy (committed use discounts, savings plans), or formal FinOps practice.

  • SLO design, alert hygiene and a Prometheus and Grafana based observability stack.

  • Real-time systems: WebSockets, WebRTC, streaming or other persistent-connection workloads.

  • Open source contributions, or writing and talks on cloud, platform or distributed systems.

Our stack

  • Go, gRPC, RocksDB, Python

  • PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ

  • GCP

  • Grafana, Prometheus, ELK (Elasticsearch and Kibana)

  • Jaeger and Tempo for distributed tracing, Datadog

  • Redis, Memcached

  • Claude Code, Cursor

You will thrive here if

  • You want platform and infrastructure problems at a scale most engineers never touch, and the autonomy to set the direction yourself.

  • You would rather try something, measure it and change course than wait for a perfect plan.

  • You ship fast and learn fast, including when it is hectic.

  • You are self-directed and comfortable working with a globally distributed team across time zones.

You probably will not if

  • You want to stay a specialist in one layer of the stack.

  • You want tightly scoped tickets and step-by-step direction.

  • You need a calm, highly predictable environment.

Compensation and benefits

For employees based in the Netherlands:

  • 28 days paid time off plus Dutch public holidays

  • Pension plan

  • Commute covered: an NS Business Card or a company Swapfiets

  • Fitness contribution of up to €60 a month toward a gym or sports club membership

  • Learning and development budget

  • Work from anywhere: up to four weeks a year

  • Full Dutch statutory leave, with Stream topping up paternity leave to 100% pay

  • Catered team lunches in the office, and snacks

  • MacBook Pro and peripherals

  • Relocation support, visa sponsorship and 30% ruling support

  • An office in the centre of Amsterdam

  • Conferences and meetups, as an attendee or a speaker

  • The chance to work on our open source SDKs

Why join Stream?

We're a Series B company with global presence and a team of around 145 people from more than 35 countries.

We're backed by Felicis Ventures, GGV Capital, 01 Advisors, Techstars, and Arthur Ventures, with angels including Dick Costolo (ex-CEO of Twitter), Olivier Pomel (CEO of Datadog), Tom Preston-Werner (co-founder of GitHub), and Nicolas Dessaigne (co-founder of Algolia).

We'll be straight with you: a startup is more demanding than a large company. There's no fixed playbook, you'll own things end to end, and you'll sometimes pick up work outside your title. That's also what makes it a fast place to grow. If you want real ownership and high scale more than structure and a set career ladder, you'll feel at home here.

The role

We're looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer I to join Stream on our mission of elevating the quality of apps for billions of users globally. You'll own the backend of our AI Moderation product: building new capabilities and making the Go services behind them cleaner, faster and more reliable.

This is a full-time role, hybrid with 3 days a week in our Toronto co-working space.

What you'll work on

You'll join our five-person Moderation team, which builds the product customers use to detect, review and act on harmful content in their apps. The role leans backend. Dedicated frontend engineers own the moderation dashboards, and you'll own the Go services, data model and integrations behind them, stepping into React when a feature spans the stack. You'll work closely with the team lead, our other Toronto-based engineer, Infrastructure, and the Customer Success and Support teams, and directly with customers' trust and safety and engineering teams.

Here's the honest current state: the product has grown fast and the backend has grown with it. There's real cleanup, refactoring and simplification to do, and you'll have the room to do it well. You'll also give the team coverage in North American hours, which today rests largely on one engineer.

Job responsibilities:

  • Build new moderation features: design and ship Go services from database schema and API endpoints through to production rollout, including work on our new AI moderation flow.

  • Clean up the backend: refactor existing moderation services, reduce technical debt, simplify code paths and raise test coverage.

  • Improve reliability and performance: strengthen alerting and observability, and fix scaling and latency issues in the moderation pipeline.

  • Own third-party integrations: maintain and extend the AI and moderation providers that plug into the pipeline.

  • Keep production healthy: diagnose defects to root cause and take part in on-call, with a focus on North American hours.

  • Work with customers: troubleshoot their issues directly and bring what you learn back into the roadmap.

  • Work across the stack when needed: ship React changes alongside the frontend engineers and review your peers' code.

About you

You're a backend engineer at heart who is comfortable picking up frontend work when a feature needs it. You enjoy leaving a codebase better than you found it, and you'd rather simplify a service than add another layer to it. You like owning problems end to end, including the ones that show up in production or in a customer conversation.

You probably won't enjoy this role if you want a pure frontend position, a large team with a fixed process, or a job with no on-call. The team is small, the product is moving fast, and North American coverage is part of the job.

Nobody at Stream has owned this media plane end to end before. Our central infrastructure team is tuned for request-based services, and video breaks in different ways: live sessions can't be dropped, bandwidth is the biggest cost, and placement is the main lever. That's why this is a Staff role. You'll set the direction for the video backend and its infrastructure with your own roadmap, reporting to our Director of Engineering with a direct line to our CTO. The Video SDK teams own the client side, and you'll work closely with them and with infrastructure. Part of the fleet is mid-move to Kubernetes.




JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Architecture: write the architecture and roadmap for Stream Video's backend and media infrastructure, and decide what ships.

 - Scale livestreaming: architect the SFU and media pipeline (WHIP, WHEP, RTMP, SRT, HLS, SVC), including the path from WebRTC to CDN-backed HLS for very large audiences.

 - Own the fleet: reliability, autoscaling, placement, rollouts, observability and cost for long-lived sessions across clouds, with cost per gigabyte as a first-class metric.

 - Gate production changes: define the validation that decides which changes, including AI-generated ones, reach live media, using behaviour tests on realistic networks, nightly telemetry scans and a public quality benchmark.

 - Take the final escalation: handle the hardest quality, latency and production incidents, and work with enterprise customers on advanced integrations.

 - Raise the bar: mentor senior engineers through design review, code review and hiring.




ABOUT YOU

You've owned systems where a dropped session or a bad rollout is visible to users within seconds, and you think about cost and reliability as much as features. You'd rather write the hard design doc than wait for one. A founder background is an asset here. The team is small, so you'll still write and review plenty of code. If you're looking for a large organisation with a platform team to hand problems to, or a management track, this role won't suit you.
